title: fix(ui): screen readers cannot tell row menu and action buttons apart
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Repeated native-catalog session menus, Sessions row menus, Worktrees actions and MCP app settings buttons had generic accessible names. Navigating by button name could not identify the target row.

Append the existing row's display name or key to each accessible name, preserving visible labels and their prefixes. Ordinary adopted OpenClaw sidebar rows already have specific names and are unchanged. Preserve Mitchell Etzel's contributor commits.

Fixes #178137.

## Evidence

[Inspected before/after screenshots and Playwright accessibility snapshots](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/178140#issuecomment-6328147202). All nine uploaded PNGs rendered successfully in Chromium.

Built production UI served by built Gateways in secretless Linux Docker: main `f365d7852ae` versus candidate `0a1f592a376`, twice for all four renderers. Real state came from sessions.create/patch, Worktrees UI against a disposable external repository, shipped MCP commands and genuine external stdio servers, and bundled native app-server thread RPCs. No OpenClaw database or catalog-response fixtures. No provider credentials or successful inference.

Main exposes repeated generic menu/Delete/App settings names. Candidate identifies Catalog Project A/B, session keys, worktree names and Parts/Notes app titles. Controls preserve ordinary adopted sidebar names, activate both row menus, delete/restore a fixture worktree and navigate both app settings targets. Browser semantics, not screen-reader speech, are proven.

Focused owner suites: 151 tests passed. Whole-diff simplification reuses existing names and action owners; no helpers, state, compatibility paths or visible-text changes. Production delta: +4/-2 lines; tests: +33/-4. The remaining string expressions are the smallest complete semantic repair.

Two-way door: reverting changes accessible names only, with no stored-state migration. Blast radius: these four repeated-action renderers and dependent test locators.
